newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hansapank dominates solid Estonian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Hansapank dominates solid Estonian share trade.

text.p: Hansapank again led a rally in busy trade on the Estonian stock exchange on Tuesday as investors rushed to buy its stock on the last day of cum-dividend trading and in view of its good first quarter results.
The Talse index rose by 1.56 percent to close on 271.77 kroons with 67.7 million kroons of shares traded on the main list.
Total market capitalisation was higher at 14.56 billion kroons compared to Monday's 14.30 billion kroons.
"The day was very busy as people were to trying to get even the smallest advantage out of the market," one trader said.
"It was not the behaviour of long-term investors," he added. "Wednesday is expected to see more sellers and volumes lower."
Hansapank turned over 36.9 million kroons to dominate trade. The stock gained 6.65 kroons to close on 286.15 kroons.
Today was the last day of cum-dividend trading in the bank's shares and also for inclusion on the list of shareholders for its bonus share issue.
"The interest in Hansapank was due to the last day for the cum-dividend trading and people hoping to make a quick profit on the bonus share issue," another trader said.
The bank also benefited from follow-on interest after it yesterday reported a sharp rise in first quarter profit.
Hoiupank saw trade of 12.5 million kroons of shares to be stable on 133.00 kroons.
"There were some large sellers on the market, but all the shares were taken up," he added.
On the over-the-counter market, total trade was 7.4 million kroons of shares with diversified industrialist Norma the most active stock.
Norma traded 2.8 millions kroons of shares to close 2.75 kroons higher on 78.50 kroons.
"The strong interest stayed with Norma after the release of the final first quarter profit figures, but the volumes on the free market were quite low," a dealer said.
Norma's adjusted first quarter net profit results were 24.2 million kroons, slightly higher than previously announced.
